text: Paulus, et Sylvanus, et Timotheus, Thessalonicensium ecclesiae, quae Dei Patris est, et Domini Jesu Christi, gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Patris* and *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20; ἐν Θεῷ πατρί, ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν, NRSV \"God the Father\", \"God our Father\"), as Gal 1:1, 1:3 and 1 Cor 1:3 *Deō Patre*; *nostrō* lower case; *grātiam* lower case: the greeting runs on in the same verse after the address's comma, as 1573 (*Domini Iesu Christi , gratiam , & pacem*, canvas 904) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Agimus immortales gratias Deo de vobis omnibus, vestri mentionem facientes in nostris precibus,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): the thanksgiving (1:2–10) after the greeting, as your Phil 1:3 and Col 1:3 open theirs with a paragraph; *precibus,* with a comma, as 1573 (*in noſtris precibus , 3 continenter*, canvas 904), for the draft's full stop: the participles of 1:3–4 (*recolentēs*, *Scientēs*) continue *Agimus*, as the Greek (μνείαν … ποιούμενοι, ἀδιαλείπτως μνημονεύοντες), so 1:3 starts in lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: continenter coram Deo Patreque nostro recolentes opus fidei vestrae, caritatisque laborem, et spei in Domino nostro Jesu Christo sitae coram Deo et Patre nostro tolerantiam:
note: *Patreque* and *Patre* capital, God the Father (τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν, NRSV \"our God and Father\"; decision 20), as Gal 1:4 *Deī, Patrisque nostrī*; *continenter* lower case, the sentence of 1:2 running on (1573 *continenter*), written here because a changed capital stops the pipeline's own lowering (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: et eius Filium ex caelis expectaretis, quem ex mortuis excitavit, Jesum, qui nos a futuro supplicio defendit.
note: *Fīlium* capital, the Son of God (τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, NRSV \"his Son\"; decision 20), as Gal 1:16 *suum Fīlium* and your Rom 8:3; *et* lower case, the sentence of 1:9 running on (1573 *& eius filium*) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Itaque nos Deo continenter gratias agimus, quod vos, accepto Dei sermone, quem a nobis audivistis, admisistis non hominum sermonem, sed (ut vere est) Dei sermonem, qui in vobis fidentibus viget.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break; the NRSV's too): 2:12 ends a sentence and *Itaque nōs Deō continenter grātiās agimus* opens the second thanksgiving (2:13–16), on how they received the word (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Itaque quum iam durare non possemus, visum est nobis Athenis relinqui solis,
note: *sōlīs,* with a comma, as 1573 (*Athenis relinqui ſolis , 2 Timotheumq; mittere*, canvas 905), for the draft's full stop: *Tīmotheumque mittere* (3:2) is the second subject of *vīsum est* (εὐδοκήσαμεν … καὶ ἐπέμψαμεν, one sentence to 3:3), so 3:2 continues the sentence (the name keeps its capital) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ipse Deus Paterque noster, et Dominus noster Jesus Christus, nostrum ad vos iter secundet:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break; the NRSV's too): 3:10's question closes the thanksgiving and *Ipse Deus* opens Paul's prayer (3:11–13); *Paterque* capital, God the Father (ὁ Θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ ἡμῶν; decision 20), *noster* lower case, as 1:3 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ut animi vestri inculpata sanctitate confirmentur in Dei Patrisque nostri conspectu, in adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi cum ejus sanctis omnibus.
note: *Patrisque* capital, God the Father (ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἡμῶν; decision 20), as Gal 1:4 *Deī, Patrisque nostrī*; *Ut* keeps its capital after 3:12's colon (settled practice) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quod ad fraternum amorem attinet, nihil opus est, ut vobis scribatur, quum vos ipsi mutuo amare divinitus didiceritis:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break; the NRSV's too): *Quod ad frāternum amōrem attinet* (Περὶ δὲ τῆς φιλαδελφίας) opens a new topic, brotherly love (4:9–12), after 4:8 closes the call to holiness, as 5:1 *Dē temporibus vērō* (Περὶ δὲ) opens its own (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vos, fratres, non estis in tenebris, ut vos dies illa tamquam fur opprimat:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 5:3 ends a sentence and *Vōs, frātrēs* (Ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί) turns from the unbelievers whom the day surprises to the readers, children of the light (5:4–8) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Hortamur item vos, fratres, castigate incompositos, solamini parum magnanimos, infirmis opitulamini, clementes este in omnes.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): after the duty toward the leaders (5:12–13), *Hortāmur item vōs, frātrēs* opens a new run of exhortations to the whole church (5:14–22), in direct address (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Adsit vobis Domini nostri Jesu Christi gratia, Amen. \\cls Ad Thessalonicenses prima scripta est Athenis.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it under the blessing (*Ad Theffalonicenses prima fcripta est Athenis .*, canvas 906) and as Gal 6:18, Col 4:18 and 2 Cor 13:14; a full stop after it, as 1573 (the draft has none); *grātia, Āmēn.* with 1573's comma, read on the page image (crop `1Thess.5.28-gratia`, canvas 906: *Christi gratia, Amen.*), for the draft's colon, as each blessing in this batch follows 1573's own stop (Claude, 2026-11-11)
